name: org.machanism.machai:machai-mcp-server
description: Machai MCP Server is a Java 17 command-line application and reusable server infrastructure for exposing Machai functional tools through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). It discovers compatible tool and prompt implementations supplied in separate runtime JARs, converts their metadata and parameter descriptors into MCP schemas, and routes client calls to the underlying functions. The server deliberately does not bundle domain tools, enabling teams to deploy their own automation, coding, data, or internal-platform capabilities independently. One entry point supports local synchronous STDIO integrations and Jetty-hosted HTTP integrations. HTTP mode supports stateless transport as well as streamable session-aware transport. Configuration includes a project directory, server name, version, port, session mode, and an optional properties file. It is suitable as an MCP gateway for desktop AI clients, remote AI agents, developer automation, and custom GenAI tool publication.

usageContext: Publish separately packaged Machai functional tools and prompts to MCP clients
Run a local STDIO server launched by a desktop MCP client
Run a remote stateless or streamable HTTP MCP endpoint
Provide a project workspace context to automation tools

constructors.description: Creates an HTTP MCP server using stateless request handling. Set its port, load tools with a configurator, and start it to serve MCP requests through Jetty.

examples.description: Creates and configures a stateless HTTP server programmatically. In normal deployments, invoke the CLI entry point so tool discovery and startup are performed automatically.

constructors.description: Creates an HTTP MCP server using streamable session-aware transport. It loads independently packaged Machai tools and prompts before accepting requests.

examples.description: Creates a streamable HTTP transport server. The equivalent supported CLI invocation uses the --port and --session options.

constructors.description: Creates a synchronous MCP server that communicates through process standard input and output, the transport used by locally launched desktop MCP clients.

examples.description: Creates a STDIO server with a workspace context. Prefer the command-line entry point for production client configuration.

features.name: main
features.signature: public static void main(java.lang.String[] args) throws java.lang.Exception
features.description: Starts the application and selects the transport. No port starts STDIO mode; --port starts stateless HTTP mode; --port with --session starts streamable HTTP mode. It also accepts project directory, configuration file, server name, and version options.

examples.snippet: java -cp machai-mcp-server.jar;team-tools.jar org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.McpServer --projectDir C:/work/app --config C:/config/mcp.properties --name team-mcp --version 1.0.0 --port 45000 --session
examples.description: Install by downloading a release or building with mvn -Ppack install, place the server JAR and a Machai functional-tool JAR on the Java classpath, provide a properties file if needed, then run a streamable HTTP MCP server on port 45000. Use : instead of ; as the classpath separator on Unix-like systems.

features.name: getConfigurator
features.signature: public static org.machanism.macha.core.commons.configurator.PropertiesConfigurator getConfigurator(java.lang.String configFile) throws java.io.IOException
features.description: Creates the properties configurator used during tool loading. A null configuration path attempts the default mcp.properties file and tolerates its absence; an explicitly supplied unreadable path causes an IOException.

examples.description: Loads an explicit tool configuration before custom server integration. CLI users achieve the same configuration by passing --config C:/config/mcp.properties.

features.name: toHumanReadable
features.description: Converts a registered Machai tool name to a lower-case kebab-case MCP-facing name, such as myToolName to my-tool-name.

examples.description: Produces the MCP tool name create-release-notes while adapting a custom tool library. This conversion is normally performed automatically during discovery.

customizations.name: Runtime functional tool libraries
customizations.description: Extend server behavior by packaging Machai-compatible functional tool and prompt implementations in separate JARs with their required service-provider registration, then adding those JARs to the runtime classpath. The server discovers and exposes them as MCP capabilities.

examples.description: Runs a server that publishes a team tool JAR through stateless HTTP MCP. Configure client access to http://localhost:45000/mcp after startup.

customizations.name: Command-line transport and context configuration
customizations.description: Use -d or --projectDir for workspace context, -c or --config for properties, -n or --name and -v or --version for metadata, -p or --port for HTTP, and -s or --session for streamable HTTP. Without -p, the application uses STDIO.

examples.description: Configures a stateless HTTP server with explicit project context and a client-visible name.

studs.name: org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.AbstractMcpServer
studs.description: Common MCP server contract that holds project-directory context and requires transport implementations to register tools and start the selected server.

studs.name: org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.AbstractMcpServer.ToolSpecificationBuilder
studs.description: Transport boundary for creating MCP-specific tool specifications from generic tool definitions and invocation handlers.

examples.title: Install and run a local STDIO MCP server
steps: Download the release JAR from SourceForge or build from source with mvn -Ppack install.
Build or obtain a Machai-compatible functional tool JAR and ensure its service-provider registration is included.
Set credentials, model settings, and other environment variables required by the selected tools.
Configure the MCP desktop client to run java -cp machai-mcp-server.jar;functional-tool-container.jar org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.McpServer.
Launch the client and verify that the discovered tools and prompts are listed.
examples.description: STDIO is the default transport because no --port option is supplied. It is intended for a local client that starts the Java process. On Unix-like systems replace the Windows classpath separator ; with :.

examples.title: Install, configure, and invoke an HTTP MCP endpoint
steps: Install Java 17 or newer and obtain the server JAR plus one or more functional tool JARs.
Create an optional mcp.properties file or prepare a configuration path required by the tools.
Connect MCP Inspector, mcp-remote, or another MCP client to http://localhost:45000/mcp.
Inspect the exposed capabilities and invoke a tool; add --session at startup when the client requires streamable HTTP transport.
examples.description: This scenario runs a stateless HTTP server and provides a known workspace to tools. Tool-specific credentials and services remain the responsibility of the deployed tool library.
